correctness.rationale: Properness localizes every color to a unique part. Looking from any other part makes the neighborhood multiplicity of that color equal to its whole class size, proving necessity of odd class sizes; the converse follows because every visible class is then seen in full with odd multiplicity. Minimizing odd class counts independently in each part gives one color for odd part size and two for even part size, hence \(r+e\). The attached exhaustive checker verifies all complete-multipartite profiles through order eight without being used for the universal proof.

evidence: The 2026 join paper determines strong odd chromatic numbers for joins of cycles with empty graphs and for one-point unions, and states that exact values are known for very few classes.

The published-finding corpus complete-multipartite record gives an exact formula for ordinary odd coloring, whose requirement is only existence of an odd-frequency color at each vertex, not odd frequency for every visible color.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The join results do not cover iterated joins of arbitrary empty graphs, and the ordinary odd-coloring theorem is for a strictly different invariant. Neither dominates the present claim.

The closest published-finding corpus complete-multipartite record concerns ordinary odd coloring rather than strong odd coloring. value.rationale: This is a complete exact classification on the canonical complete-multipartite family. It sharpens the foundational complete-bipartite upper bound to a parity-exact \(2/3/4\) law and extends it to any number of parts, while giving a reusable structural criterion for all strong odd colorings in the class. The direction is directly motivated by recent exact work on joins and is not an arbitrary parameter slice.
